title: Canonical ordinary module obtained by restricting an algebraic-space module to an etale scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $q:h_T\to F$ an object of its small etale site. For any module sheaf $M$ on that site, define its ordinary $\mathcal O_T$-module $q^*_{\mathrm{Zar}}M$ by restriction to open subschemes: its sections on $U\subseteq T$ are $M(h_U\to h_T\to F)$, with the given restriction maps and with scalars transported through the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_T(U)\simeq\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. More precisely the functor from Zariski opens of $T$ sends $U$ to the composite $h_U\to h_T\to F$; these composites are representable etale, and this inclusion is continuous for the Zariski and small-etale topologies. Restriction along this continuous functor and the canonical structure-ring comparison defines $q^*_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ on modules and module maps. This is the restriction-to-opens interpretation of a line module on a scheme; no descent object or arbitrary comparison is chosen.

source.place: Tag 03ED (small etale site) and Tag 03G7 (structure sheaf); descent.tex Tag 03FH (remark-change-topologies-ringed-sites), and Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent): the inverse comparison is restriction to Zariski opens.
